title: Rotational kernel priority decay incident - postmortem and remediation
creator: Miguel Alvarez
description: Summary: During a high-concurrency capacity event on 2026-03-09 we observed a sustained P95/P99 latency regression for multi-tenant hosted workloads. The root mechanism was a subtle interaction in the scheduler's rotational kernel priority decay heuristic: kernels that were temporarily deprioritized (to favor fused/quantized paths) accumulated decay and were not re-promoted cleanly, causing a class of requests to be routed to suboptimal execution paths and experience long tails. This document captures the detection timeline, analysis, mitigations taken, and actionable follow-ups.
detection_timeline:
2026-03-09 02:12 UTC - Alerts: Per-route P95 spikes triggered by Console.
2026-03-09 02:20 UTC - Oncall triage confirmed elevation in error budgets for a subset of models and increased instance CPU on workers handling fallback kernels.
2026-03-09 02:45 UTC - Narrowed to kernel assignment skew; synthetic repro in staging at 03:10 reproduced high tail when rotational decay parameter at runtime drifted.
2026-03-09 04:00 UTC - Emergency mitigation deployed (temporary clamp on priority decay and canary rollback for scheduler change).
impact_summary: Impacted hosted API customers using medium/long context generation at 20-40 concurrent requests per second. Measured effects: median latency unchanged, P95 increased by ~2.6x and P99 by ~4x for affected routes for ~2.5 hours, increased token cost due to repeated fallback execution, and operationally elevated CPU on fallback executors. No data loss or correctness regressions observed.
root_cause: The scheduler uses a rotational priority decay to prevent hot-kernel monopolization. A recent change introduced a non-idempotent state update where kernels that were demoted would accumulate decay in a way that persisted past expected rebalancing windows. Under sustained load with oscillating model shapes (mixed short/long sequences) this caused a cohort of kernels to remain deprioritized and forced requests onto slower execution paths. Contributing factors: insufficient hysteresis in re-promotion logic, lack of a determinism test in the kernel scorer, and gaps in alerting for kernel-class imbalance.
mitigation_and_timeline: Immediate: rolled back scheduler heuristics to the previous stable release and applied a temporary clamp on decay accumulation (2026-03-09 04:05 UTC). Mid-term: reverted the non-idempotent state update and added a safety check to bound decay per-kernel (2026-03-10). Long-term: redesign the priority rotation to use a convex smoothing function with deterministic seeding and guardrails; schedule below action items for implementation.
action_items: ENG-841211 - Implement deterministic kernel scoring unit tests (owner: Asha Patel, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-21)
ENG-841212 - Add hysteresis and bounded decay per-kernel; replace additive decay with convex smoothing (owner: Rohit Sengupta, estimate: 5, due: 2026-03-28)
ENG-841213 - Integrate kernel-class imbalance alerting into Console with runbook (owner: Slo Ops team - Priya Nair, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-841214 - Create deterministic canary for scheduler changes that includes synthetic mixed-shape workload (owner: Performance QA - Lina Zhou, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-24)
ENG-841215 - Add integration test to CI that asserts no persistent decay beyond 2 rebalancing cycles (owner: CI infra - Mateo Ruiz, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-20)
ENG-841216 - Run retro with SRE/Support to update incident detection thresholds and postmortem learnings (owner: Miguel Alvarez, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-17)
ENG-841217 - Benchmark and document cost impact of fallback routing; add cost visibility per-route in Optimize (owner: Product - Sara Kim, estimate: 3, due: 2026-04-01)
qa_plan: Create synthetic mixed-short-long workload generator that reproduces scheduler-induced skew in staging
Run nightly stress test for 72 hours with new bounded-decay implementation and assert no >1.5x P95 regressions versus baseline
Add regression guard in PRs changing scheduler heuristics that executes the generator as a fast smoke test
monitoring_and_alerting: New metric: kernel_assignment_entropy (per-host, per-model) - alert when entropy < threshold for 5m
New alert: persistent_decay_ratio > 0.25 for 10m triggers P0 escalation
Dashboard: Kernel health view with decay distribution and fallback routing rate by model and region
rollout_plan: Canary rollout in us-west-2 on 10% of traffic for 6 hours with automatic rollback on P95 > 1.3x baseline
Gradual ramp to 50% over 24 hours while monitoring kernel_assignment_entropy and CPU per-worker
Full rollout after 72h stable canary and signoff from performance QA and SRE
notes: This incident highlights subtle statefulness in scheduler heuristics that appears harmless at low concurrency but amplifies under mixed-shape workloads. Priority: harden determinism and observability before next scheduler heuristic release.
followup_review: Schedule in retro cadence: 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC with SRE and Support. Required attendees: owners of action items. Deliverable: close each sub-issue or provide status update.
customer_communication: Proactive note sent to affected customers on 2026-03-10 summarizing impact and remediation steps; follow-up with detailed RCA planned after action items complete.
